judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The image is the only content of a news-card link to the story 'Ouvidor nacional de Justiça reforça atuação proativa e acessível das ouvidorias judiciais'. Its alt names the CNJ counsellor and national ombudsman Marcello Terto e Silva speaking in a lecture at the IV Encontro de Ouvidores e Ouvidoras Judiciais da Região Norte; I opened the destination and the story is the report of exactly that keynote lecture by him at that event. Read as the link text under the 'NOTÍCIAS' heading, the alternative names the story's subject, so by R2's first step it describes the link's purpose and the link passes 1.1.1 on this point (the extra stage detail does not hide the purpose). The claim that it does not say where the link leads is therefore not true of the capture. The live page serves the same alt and link, so the capture does not differ. Rampa had the destination title and judged wrongly: model_error.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: [visual context] This is the 'Leia mais' link of the second visible news card ('Saber ouvir tornou-se uma competência indispensável', destaca presidente do TJTO...). The three 'Leia mais' links in the accessibility tree (slides 4-6; the other twelve slick slides and clones are aria-hidden with their links taken out of the tab order) all have the accessible name 'Leia mais...' from aria-label, no title and no aria-describedby. Each sits alone in div.readmore; the card headline is a separate link in span.newsflash-title, not in the same sentence, paragraph, list item or table cell, and not a heading. The slide wrapper is role=option inside a role=listbox, which is not a list item. The heading just before all three is the same h3 'NOTÍCIAS', so their contexts are identical and they form one set. They lead to three different news stories (non-equivalent resources), and each card's visible headline and photo tell them apart, so by R1 every link of the set fails 2.4.4. The claim (three links, three places, nothing around it tells it apart) is true of the capture and names that failure; no link carries another's name, the generic aria-label shared by every card is the defect. The live HTML has the same aria-label and structure, so the capture does not differ.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The page is the landing page of the TJTO Ouvidoria Judiciária and its title is only 'Apresentação' (the live page sends the same title). The word matches the h1 and says the page is an introduction, so 'says nothing about this page' overstates it; but it does not name the subject (the Ouvidoria or the court), does not make sense out of context, and fails G88's check that the page can be identified from its title: I fetched /apoio-as-vitimas, /cogersa, /ouvidoria-mulher, /coges and /ouvidoria/ouvidoria-da-mulher on the same site and all are titled 'Apresentação' as well. Tabs, history or search results for these pages cannot be told apart, which is what 2.4.2 is meant to prevent (close to F25). Read in good faith, the claim points at this non-descriptive title, so the label is true_positive. No capture difference.
